bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42526050 (PcapPlusPlus): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 2 found by fuzz target FuzzTarget [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42526050
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source / static parse of the staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is a 124-byte little-endian pcap with global-header linktype 239 (LINKTYPE_NFLOG) and first-packet caplen 82, so packet parsing enters `NflogLayer`. At packet offset 4 the first TLV bytes are `01 00 09 00`, so `getTlvByType(NFULA_PAYLOAD)` materializes that TLV and `NflogTlv::getTotalSize()` returns raw `recordLen == 1` on the reproduced little-endian build. `payloadLen = getTotalSize() - 4` therefore wraps to `SIZE_MAX-2`, while `payload` points at packet offset 8. Because that byte is `0x46`, NFLOG accepts the span as IPv4. `IPv4Layer::initLayerInPacket()` then sees `totalLength == 0` and keeps the wrapped extent, and `IPv4Layer::parseNextLayer()` computes `hdrLen == 24`, `payloadLen = m_DataLen - hdrLen`, and constructs `new UdpLayer(payload, payloadLen, ...)`. `UdpLayer::parseNextLayer()` subtracts the 8-byte UDP header to derive a huge `udpDataLen`, sees destination port 53, and constructs `DnsLayer` with that bogus extent. The DNS header bytes decode as `QDCOUNT=0`, `ANCOUNT=4`, `NSCOUNT=0`, `ARCOUNT=0`, so `DnsLayer::parseResources()` walks bogus zero-filled answers; after two 11-byte answers, the third answer starts at DNS offset 34. In `DnsResource::getDataLength()`, `sizeToRead` is 9 and the guard compares `34 + 9` against the wrapped DNS length instead of the real 42 captured DNS bytes, so it falls through to `*(uint16_t*)(getRawData() + sizeToRead)`. That load is issued from packet offset 83, and Stage 01's AddressSanitizer trace reports it as a heap-buffer-overflow read in `DnsResource.cpp:297` against the 82-byte allocation made by `PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()`. The fix's alignment change in `NflogTlv::getTotalSize()` is sufficient to close this witness by turning raw `recordLen == 1` into aligned size 4, making `payloadLen` 0 instead of wrapping; the simultaneous `assign()` cleanup change is present in the patch but is not needed to explain this PoC.

source.description: Source. NFLOG parsing materializes the attacker-controlled payload TLV view from the first TLV bytes of the 82-byte packet.
source.value_from: A static parse of the staged `gt_results/arvo_42526050/poc` shows a pcap global-header linktype of 239 (NFLOG), first-packet caplen 82, and packet bytes `01 00 09 00` at offsets 4-7. This statement asks the NFLOG TLV reader for `NFULA_PAYLOAD`, so the returned `payloadInfo` aliases those exact attacker-controlled bytes.
source.note: This is the first project statement on the vulnerable path that turns the malformed NFLOG packet bytes into vulnerability-relevant parser state after the outer pcap container has already been admitted.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. NFLOG TLV size derivation returns the raw 16-bit `recordLen` with no 4-byte alignment or minimum-size enforcement, so the malformed payload TLV contributes a total size of 1 byte even though the TLV header itself is 4 bytes.
root_cause.note: The staged fix changes this exact method to `return align<4>(m_Data->recordLen);`. On this witness, raw bytes `01 00` become total size 1 here; the aligned fixed code would normalize that to 4, making the downstream `payloadLen` calculation zero instead of underflowing. The patch also changes `assign()`, but this PoC closes on the alignment change alone.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The third fabricated DNS answer reads its 2-byte `dataLength` field past the 82-byte packet allocation.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at this exact line, with callers `getSize` and `pcpp::DnsLayer::parseResources`.

parser_admitted.description: The misframed bytes have already passed NFLOG and IPv4 parsing, and UDP dispatch admits them into `DnsLayer` because destination port 53 and the wrapped `udpDataLen` satisfy DNS parsing.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant tainted scalar is the NFLOG payload TLV length. On the reproduced little-endian build, this method reads raw bytes `01 00` as host-endian value 1 and returns it unchanged.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Static parsing of the staged 82-byte NFLOG packet shows TLV bytes `01 00 09 00` at packet offsets 4-7, so this method sees `recordLen` bytes `01 00` and `recordType` bytes `09 00` in the first TLV, yielding `recordLen == 1` and `recordType == 9 (NFULA_PAYLOAD)` on the reproduced host.
tainted_value_origin.note: That under-sized length is reused as the basis for the NFLOG payload span and, after successive unsigned subtractions, as the effective IPv4, UDP, and DNS layer extent that defeats the downstream DNS bounds check.

fine_trace.note: Source step. `parseNextLayer()` asks the NFLOG TLV reader for `NFULA_PAYLOAD`. On the exact witness, the first TLV bytes at packet offsets 4-7 are `01 00 09 00`, so `payloadInfo` becomes a view over attacker-controlled bytes that already claim `recordType == 9`.

Root-cause step. For the `payloadInfo` object from step 1, this method reads raw bytes `01 00` as host-endian value 1 on the reproduced little-endian build and returns total size 1 without NFLOG's required 4-byte alignment or any check that the size is at least the 4-byte TLV header.

fine_trace.code:
uint8_t* payload = payloadInfo.getValue();
size_t payloadLen = payloadInfo.getTotalSize() - sizeof(uint16_t) * 2;
fine_trace.note: Subtracting the 4-byte TLV header from the 1-byte total size from step 2 underflows `payloadLen` to `SIZE_MAX-2` (`18446744073709551613` on the reproduced 64-bit build). `payload` itself points at packet offset 8, where the first byte is `0x46`.

fine_trace.code:
case PCPP_WS_NFPROTO_IPV4:
	m_NextLayer = IPv4Layer::isDataValid(payload, payloadLen)
		? static_cast<Layer*>(new IPv4Layer(payload, payloadLen, this, m_Packet))
		: static_cast<Layer*>(new PayloadLayer(payload, payloadLen, this, m_Packet));
fine_trace.note: NFLOG header byte `0x02` selects the IPv4 branch, and `IPv4Layer::isDataValid(payload, payloadLen)` succeeds because the byte at packet offset 8 is `0x46` (IPv4, IHL 6) while `payloadLen` from step 3 is huge. The misframed payload is therefore constructed as an `IPv4Layer` instead of being left as opaque payload.

The fabricated IPv4 header bytes at the `payload` pointer encode `totalLength == 0`. That makes the clamp predicate false, so `IPv4Layer` keeps `m_DataLen` as the huge wrapped extent from step 4 (`18446744073709551613`) instead of reducing it to the actually captured bytes.

The IPv4 byte `0x46` gives header length 24, so `hdrLen == 24`. The early return is bypassed because the wrapped `m_DataLen` from step 5 is far larger than 24, and `payloadLen` becomes `18446744073709551589`. `payload` now points at packet offset 32, the start of the UDP header.

The IPv4 protocol byte is `0x11`, so this UDP branch fires. The constructor call passes the huge `payloadLen` from step 6 as `UdpLayer`'s `dataLen`, which is the source of the UDP layer extent used next.

fine_trace.code:
uint8_t* udpData = m_Data + sizeof(udphdr);
size_t udpDataLen = m_DataLen - sizeof(udphdr);
fine_trace.note: Because the `UdpLayer` from step 7 inherited the huge `dataLen`, subtracting the 8-byte UDP header produces `udpDataLen == 18446744073709551581`. `udpData` points at packet offset 40, where the DNS header begins.

fine_trace.code:
else if (DnsLayer::isDataValid(udpData, udpDataLen) && (DnsLayer::isDnsPort(portDst) || DnsLayer::isDnsPort(portSrc)))
	m_NextLayer = new DnsLayer(udpData, udpDataLen, this, m_Packet);
fine_trace.note: At packet offset 32 the UDP header bytes decode as source port 11264 and destination port 53. Because `udpDataLen` from step 8 is huge, `DnsLayer::isDataValid(udpData, udpDataLen)` succeeds, and this branch constructs `DnsLayer` with the same wrapped extent instead of stopping at UDP payload bounds.

The first 12 DNS bytes at `udpData` decode as `QDCOUNT=0`, `ANCOUNT=4`, `NSCOUNT=0`, `ARCOUNT=0`, so `numOfOtherResources` becomes 4. `parseResources()` therefore commits to parsing four resource records rather than stopping after the fixed DNS header.

Because step 10 committed to four records, `parseResources()` keeps instantiating answers in zero-filled bytes. The first two answers parse as root-name records with `m_NameLength == 1`, `getDataLength() == 0`, and `getSize() == 11`, so `offsetInPacket` advances `12 -> 23 -> 34`. On the third answer, this line reaches DNS offset 34 and `newResource->getSize()` enters `DnsResource::getDataLength()` for that record.

For the third fabricated answer, `m_OffsetInLayer == 34` and the zero name byte gives `m_NameLength == 1`, so `sizeToRead == 9`. The guard compares `34 + 9 == 43` against the wrapped DNS extent inherited from step 9 (`18446744073709551581`), so it stays false even though only 42 DNS bytes actually exist inside the 82-byte packet.

Sink. After step 12 leaves the guard open, this 2-byte load is issued from packet offset 83. Stage 01's ASan trace reports that address as 1 byte to the right of the 82-byte heap region allocated in `PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()`, matching the saved `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at `DnsResource.cpp:297`.

crash_stack.function: pcpp::DnsLayer::DnsLayer(unsigned char*, unsigned long, pcpp::Layer*, pcpp::Packet*)

poc.trigger: Stage 01 saved `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42526050 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` in `pcpp::DnsResource::getDataLength() const` via `pcpp::DnsLayer::parseResources()` and `pcpp::UdpLayer::parseNextLayer()`.

format.name: pcap / LINKTYPE_NFLOG
format.contract: This exact staged pcap witness has global-header linktype 239 (NFLOG), first-packet caplen 82, and first-packet bytes `01 00 09 00` at offsets 4-7, so vulnerable NFLOG parsing treats the first TLV as `NFULA_PAYLOAD` with `recordLen == 1`. The bytes at payload offset 8 simultaneously satisfy IPv4 version/IHL checks, carry IPv4 `totalLength == 0`, decode as UDP with destination port 53, and decode the following 12 bytes as DNS with `ANCOUNT == 4`, reaching the saved third-answer over-read.
